focus: Pi: hooks, tool names, install/update/rollback, compaction path, deny/rewrite/replace, subagent handling, project source, skills, v1 footprint

findings.claim: ADR-0004's own Context section says Pi passes MCP `instructions` ('Pi: first line only, through its MCP path'), but the same ADR's Decision 5 says Pi runs as an in-process plugin, not over MCP, and gets routing text through its plugin mechanism instead.
findings.evidence: docs/v2/adr/0004-no-skills-mcp-instructions.md:32 'Pi: first line only, through its MCP path.' vs line 53 'Pi runs as an in-process plugin, not over MCP. It gets the same instructions.md bytes through its single plugin mechanism.' TECH-SPEC.md:177 and :83 (v2 runs Pi as an in-process plugin, not over MCP) and tickets/v2-decisions.md line 83 ('Over MCP: [V] first line only ... v2 runs Pi as an in-process plugin, not over MCP, so this path is not used') agree with Decision 5, not with line 32. Line 32 is leftover v1-era phrasing describing the old MCP-based Pi integration (pi-mono extensions/mcp runtime), not the v2 design.
findings.archaeology: n/a (doc-internal contradiction, not a v1 regression)
findings.fix: Delete or reword ADR-0004 line 32 to match Decision 5 and TECH-SPEC:83/:177: Pi does not receive `instructions` over MCP in v2; it gets the same bytes via its in-process `before_agent_start` plugin hook.

findings.claim: No ADR or TECH-SPEC decision states how v2 resolves Pi's project source (cwd/worktree); the only evidence on file (spike-project-source.md) describes the v1/MCP mechanism, which the project explicitly decided NOT to use for Pi in v2.
findings.evidence: tickets/spike-project-source.md:25: 'Pi | `roots/list` (built-in MCP); our bridge: env from `ctx.cwd` | verified | pi-mono packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/mcp/runtime.ts:364'. That `roots/list` path is MCP-only. TECH-SPEC.md:83/:177 and ADR-0004 Decision 5 state v2 runs Pi in-process, not over MCP, so `roots/list` cannot be the v2 mechanism. ADR-0010:46 (D7 'project and worktree | resolved from the agent's single source') and ADR-0007:74 (Q11, one named project source per host) never list Pi or its in-process equivalent. The only in-process cwd handle on file is `ctx.cwd` from the extension API (tickets/spike-hooks-verified.md:45), but no doc wires that into D7 or Q11 for Pi.
findings.archaeology: n/a (Pi is third-party source, no v1 history to check; this is a v2-design gap)
findings.fix: Add a Pi row to ADR-0010's D7 check and ADR-0007's Q11 project-source table: resolve project/worktree from the extension API's `ctx.cwd` at plugin-load time (not via `roots/list`/MCP), and add a live check verifying it matches the host's actual cwd across worktrees.

findings.claim: ADR-0016's Pi row for Case C ('replace result in-process') is asserted without naming the exact API field, even though the Pi extension types shipped in this workspace can confirm or refute it precisely.
findings.evidence: ADR-0016 line 40: 'Pi, OpenCode 2 | yes | mutate input in-process | replace result in-process'. Checked against pi-mono packages/coding-agent/src/core/extensions/types.ts:1267-1283 (ToolResultEventBase: `content`, `structuredContent`, `details` are all handler-mutable fields on the `tool_result` event) and types.ts:1454-1457 (`ToolCallEventResult.block`/`reason`, and 'To modify arguments, mutate `event.input` in place instead.'). The claim is directionally correct (tool_result handlers can rewrite `content`/`structuredContent` in place) but the ADR cites no field name, so a future implementer could drop `structuredContent` when redacting `content` -- which the Pi type comment itself calls out: 'Handlers that redact `content` should also replace this; replacing `content` alone drops it.'
findings.archaeology: n/a (Pi source, not v1 cm-main history)
findings.fix: Cite the exact fields in ADR-0016's Pi row: mutate `event.input` in place pre-call (tool_call), and set `content` AND `structuredContent` together post-call (tool_result) to avoid the drop the Pi API docs warn about.

findings.claim: ADR-0011's npm-to-git migration guidance for Pi tells the user to edit `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`, but gives no detection check (D4/ctx_doctor) that would catch a user who still has the old `npm:context-mode` entry alongside the new git entry.
findings.evidence: ADR-0011:69 'Pi | `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` `packages[]` `"npm:context-mode"`; data `~/.pi/context-mode/` | Replace with the git entry'. ADR-0010's D4 check only says 'v1 leftovers | the ADR-0011 detect function; each finding is listed with its fix' (docs/v2/adr/0010-doctor-and-upgrade.md:28) without naming Pi's `packages[]` array as one of the detect targets, unlike the explicit per-agent entries the same ADR gives for other hosts.
findings.archaeology: n/a (forward-looking migration gap, no prior v1 commit to cite since Pi is new to the adapter table)
findings.fix: Add Pi's `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` `packages[]` containing `npm:context-mode` to ADR-0011's detect-function target list and to ADR-0010's D4 check table, so `ctx_doctor` flags a stale npm entry even after the git entry is added, matching the 'two install trees' failure class (#901) the same ADR already names for other agents.
